title: Ya sea... ya sea: presentar dos opciones formales

sections.content: Ya sea... ya sea (whether... or, be it... or) formally presents two alternative methods or paths without ranking one above the other -- a natural fit for describing how the superpowers pursued the same goal (containment, expansion of influence) through more than one channel at once. These sentences are taken directly from the previous reading.

items.spanish: Ya sea a través de alianzas militares formales, ya sea mediante ayuda económica condicionada, ambas superpotencias buscaron sumar países a su propio bloque.
items.english: Whether through formal military alliances or through conditional economic aid, both superpowers sought to add countries to their own bloc.

items.spanish: Debía impedirse, ya sea mediante presión diplomática, ya sea mediante intervención militar directa, la expansión del comunismo.
items.english: The expansion of communism had to be prevented, whether through diplomatic pressure or through direct military intervention.

items.spanish: Ambas superpotencias poseían arsenales capaces de destruir, ya sea de manera directa, ya sea a través de sus efectos posteriores, la civilización humana varias veces.
items.english: Both superpowers possessed arsenals capable of destroying human civilization several times over, whether directly or through their aftereffects.

items.spanish: La región se convirtió, casi inevitablemente, en uno de los escenarios más activos de la Guerra Fría.
items.english: The region became, almost inevitably, one of the most active stages of the Cold War.

sections.content: Ya sea stays invariable in both slots (never ya sean, even with a plural noun following) -- it's a fixed connector, not a verb agreeing with what comes after it.
